Usage: emlf [--no-prelude] [-i DIR ...] [--type] [FILE | --expr SOURCE]
       emlf --check [XMLF_FILE]
       emlf [--no-prelude] [-i DIR ...] --run [FILE | --expr SOURCE] [-- ARG ...]
       emlf --run-xmlf [XMLF_FILE] [-- ARG ...]
       emlf [--no-prelude] [-i DIR ...] --emit-llvm [FILE | --expr SOURCE]
       emlf --xmlf-to-llvm [XMLF_FILE]
       emlf [--no-prelude] [-i DIR ...] --emit-llvm-gc [FILE | --expr SOURCE]
       emlf --xmlf-to-llvm[-io]-gc [XMLF_FILE]
       emlf --llvm-runtime
With no FILE, read eMLF from standard input.
Imports load Foo.Bar from Foo/Bar.emlf beside the entry or in -i search roots.
The standard prelude supplies Monad and Monad IO; --no-prelude disables it.
Link LLVM IR with clang, runtime/mlf_runtime.c, and GMP.
The -gc commands require the runtime built with MLF_USE_BDWGC and MLF_COMPACT_BDWGC.

methodology.compile: Fresh source-to-executable builds. MLF uses the general compile_native.py driver: LLVM emission/IR writes and fresh runtime C compilation overlap, followed by LLVM compilation and linking. At most two compiler processes overlap within an MLF build; samples/languages remain serial. Tool/compiler/harness setup excluded. Fresh output directory per sample; no object cache. Rotating language order.
methodology.runtime: All binaries built and checked before any timed samples; exact runtime input checked once before timing as warmup. Process startup/IO/GC/exit included. Output checked again after each sample, outside timing. No time subtraction.
methodology.resource_measurement: wait4 child usage: user+system CPU; Darwin RSS bytes, Linux RSS KiB converted to bytes. Pipeline CPU summed, RSS maximum over stages (largest child peak, not simultaneous aggregate memory).
methodology.normalization: Wall medians divided by C wall median; ratio below 1 is allowed.

input_integrity: All recorded source, manifest, harness, compiler and runtime hashes unchanged
